#### §20: Signals

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-20.1 | §20.1 | HIST | **One** reserved real-time signal (32), multiplexing cancellation and credential broadcast with a per-thread request word. `SIGEV_THREAD` timers need no signal (D-23.3). So `SIGRTMIN` = 33 (observable; programs obtain it through `__libc_current_sigrtmin`). OD-8 records the fallback of reserving two. **Verified 2026-10-04 (OD-8 ruling):** `conformance/c/s20_internal_signal.c` (run by clause tests `s20_1_c_2`, `s20_2_f_0`, `s20_3_g_0`) reads the kernel's mask and action raw after every route: `sigprocmask`, `pthread_sigmask`, `sigblock`, `sigsetmask`, an action's `sa_mask`, `setcontext`/`swapcontext` masks, `signalfd`, `sigsuspend`, `sigwaitinfo`/`sigtimedwait`, `posix_spawn` `SETSIGMASK` never block 32; `sigaction`, `signal`, `sigset`, `sigignore`, `sighold`, `sigrelse`, `siginterrupt` on 32 are `EINVAL`; no reported set (masks, `sa_mask`, `sigpending`, spawn attributes, `getcontext`) contains it; it has no name and no real-time text. Two fixes: `setcontext` and `swapcontext` installed the context's mask as given (a context mask with bit 32 blocked it); they now install a copy with 32 cleared (`machine/context.S`). `raise(32)` is `EINVAL` (it was sent; glibc refuses its own internal signals in `raise`, `pthread_kill`, `pthread_sigqueue`). `kill`, `tgkill`, `sigqueue` and `killpg` stay the kernel's, as glibc's: 32 sent to a Liella process reaches the library's handler, which ignores a signal without a request. (Amended by D-20.9.) |
| D-20.2 | §20.2 | KERN | The restorer trampoline is a C-layer machine primitive (`machine/restorer.S`, ⚑ KERN). Internal dispositions are a typed enum in `rt::signal`. |
| D-20.3 | §20.3 | ARB, HIST | **Internal:** `SigSet` is a `u64`. **Boundary:** `sigset_t` stays 128 bytes (ABI). Bits beyond 64 read as zero and are ignored on input. |
| D-20.4 | §20.2 | HIST | `signal` has BSD semantics. `sysv_signal`, `sigset`/`sighold`/`sigrelse`/`sigignore`, `sigvec`, `sigblock` and the two `sigpause` forms are legacy translations. |
| D-20.5 | §20.9 | HIST | The internal preferred interface is `SignalStream` (signalfd-backed) for synchronous handling. |
| D-20.6 | §20.2 | KERN | **IP-16's "dispatch table" (accepted 2026-10-01):** user handlers are installed in the kernel directly, with the library's restorer, and the kernel's record is the only copy of a user disposition (no table that could drift from it, for example after `SA_RESETHAND`). The rt table holds the library's own handler for the internal signal, which phase 6 installs. |
| D-20.7 | §20.2, §20.3 | HIST | C `struct sigaction` and the 1024-bit `sigset_t` are converted in `legacy::signal_compat`. The ABI crate models `sa_handler`/`sa_sigaction` as a union whose fields only `unsafe` code may read, so legacy defines `CSigaction` with the same layout (tested). The internal signal is never set, blocked, reported, accepted by a wait, or put into a filled set. |
| D-20.8 | §20.4 | HIST | **`pthread_kill` and `pthread_sigqueue` (milestone 5, 2026-10-04).** Both target one thread through `tgkill`/`rt_tgsigqueueinfo`; signal 0 only checks; an invalid signal (and the internal signal 32, D-20.1) is `EINVAL` returned with `errno` untouched. A thread that has exited but not been joined: `pthread_kill` returns 0 and sends nothing, as §20.4's Failure clause says for 2.34+ (**found and fixed:** it returned `ESRCH`, including when the thread exits between the lookup and `tgkill`); `pthread_sigqueue` returns `ESRCH`, as the reference does and pthread_sigqueue(3) says ("thread is not valid"). `conformance/c/s20_pthread_kill.c` checks all of it and passes against the reference too (clauses `s20_4_c_5`, `s20_4_f_0`). |
| D-20.9 | §20.1 | — | **The internal signal's handler is installed lazily, by the first thread creation** (owner ruling #7075, 2026-11-20: "Make it lazy is fine"; amends D-20.1 and OD-8's install-at-start). The library sends signal 32 only to a thread it created (a cancellation request to another thread, the setxid broadcast), so thread creation installs the handler before its first clone, once per process (a fork child inherits handler and flag); a start, static or dynamic, makes no `rt_sigaction`. The reservation is unchanged and fixed from start-up (OD-8): no mask blocks or reports 32 and `sigaction` on 32 is `EINVAL`. The one behaviour change: a raw 32 sent to the process before its first thread ends it (the default action). `conformance/c/s20_internal_signal.c` checks the default action at start, the handler after the first `pthread_create`, and the absorb cases after it. |
| D-20.10 | §20.7 | HIST, KERN | **`MINSIGSTKSZ` and `SIGSTKSZ` are constants or run-time values in exactly the configurations the reference's are, with the reference's values** (owner ruling 2026-11-24, final: "yes, match glibc, with that qualification": a constant exactly where the reference has one, a run-time value exactly where it has one; HEADERS-SMALL-FIXES-2 ruling item #8417). Without `_GNU_SOURCE` or `_DYNAMIC_STACK_SIZE_SOURCE` both are integer constant expressions (2048 and 8192, Appendix C), so a static array size or a `constexpr` compiles; with either (and in C++, where g++ predefines `_GNU_SOURCE`) both expand to `__sysconf (_SC_SIGSTKSZ)` (the call declared under the reserved name, as HEADERS-SMALL-FIXES did), so such a use fails to compile with libniji as with the reference (older Catch2 is the known case) and no program rebuilt against libniji gets less alternate-stack room than with the reference. Spec s20_7_i_0 and the 2.34 release notes give `MINSIGSTKSZ` as `sysconf (_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ)` (the kernel's minimum: 3632 on the Skylake-SP host, 1776 on the Zen 1 host); the reference evaluates it to `SIGSTKSZ`'s value (14528 and 8192 there), so libniji follows the reference and the disagreement is spec/ERRATA.md E14. Probe matrix (black box, compile and run, reference and libniji, Zen 1 and Skylake-SP hosts; constant = a file-scope array (C) or `constexpr` (C++) compiles): handoff/HEADERS-SIGSTKSZ-MATCH.md. Tests: the `value` unit of `spec/tools/header_checks/s08.py` in every configuration where a header shows the macros (constant configurations: the values; run-time ones: not a constant and the `_SC_SIGSTKSZ` name), and `conformance/c/s20_sigstksz_dynamic.c` (both equal `sysconf (_SC_SIGSTKSZ)` at run time, built against either header set). |
